text:
Posters for burgers, sweets and fizzy drinks surround children on screens and streets, and some believe that governments should limit advertising of unhealthy food. I agree to a large extent, since such advertising shapes children's choices and fuels obesity, although education must go with it.

To begin with, governments should restrict advertising of unhealthy food because it shapes children's choices. Repeated adverts for sweets and fast food make them attractive and normal. A child who sees a burger advertised during every cartoon, for example, will ask for it, and food companies spend huge sums on this because it works. Obesity and type two diabetes are rising rapidly among young people, which costs health services billions and shortens lives. Experiments show that children who watch such adverts eat more snacks immediately afterwards. Limiting broadcast times and locations reduces demand, and countries that have banned such advertising before nine in the evening or near schools have recorded reductions in the purchase of unhealthy products.

However, advertising limits alone are not sufficient, and they raise questions about freedom of trade. Companies argue that their products are legal and that consumers are responsible for their own choices. Parents also have a role in shaping habits at home. Education should therefore accompany restrictions: schools can teach nutrition and cooking, labelling can show sugar and fat clearly, and healthy food should be made cheaper and easier to find. Taxes on sugary drinks have also encouraged manufacturers to reduce sugar. When these measures are combined, public health costs fall and children grow up with better habits.

In conclusion, I agree that governments should limit the advertising of unhealthy food, as long as this is part of a wider strategy for healthy living.

plan.think: Mở bài nêu áp phích burger, kẹo, nước ngọt bao quanh trẻ; largely agree.

Quảng cáo định hình lựa chọn của trẻ: lặp lại làm hấp dẫn và bình thường; ví dụ trẻ thấy burger quảng cáo mỗi phim hoạt hình sẽ đòi; công ty chi khổng lồ vì hiệu quả; béo phì, tiểu đường tăng, tốn tỷ cho y tế; thí nghiệm ăn vặt nhiều hơn; hạn chế giờ phát sóng, địa điểm giảm cầu; nước cấm trước 9 giờ tối hoặc gần trường.

Chỉ hạn chế chưa đủ, đụng tự do thương mại: công ty cho là hợp pháp, người tiêu dùng chịu trách nhiệm; cha mẹ; giáo dục: dinh dưỡng, nấu ăn, nhãn đường, chất béo, đồ lành mạnh rẻ; thuế nước ngọt; chi phí y tế giảm.
Đồng ý nếu là chiến lược rộng.
